questions.answer: Tuple is ordered + immutable; list is ordered + mutable. Both indexed/sliced/mixed-type. Tuple has only count/index; hashable if all elements hashable so usable as dict key; list unhashable.
questions.question: Compare tuple vs list and when to use each.

questions.answer: Comma defines tuple: `(10,)` and `10,` are tuples, `(10)` is int, `()` empty. Unpack positionally `n,a,r=user` (counts must match else ValueError); `first,*mid,last` starred collects list; enables loop unpack and `a,b=b,a` swap.
questions.question: Explain single-element tuple gotcha and extended unpacking.

questions.answer: Tuple refs immutable but pointed-to objects may mutate: `data=([1,2],[3,4]); data[0].append(5)` works, `data[0]=x` TypeErrors. `return a,b` returns a tuple; unpack `n,a=get()`. Only hashable tuples (no lists inside) work as dict keys.
questions.question: Can a tuple's contents change? How do tuples work with functions and dict keys?

questions.answer: `x=(10)` is int — needs comma `(10,)`. `*middle` from tuple unpack is a list, not tuple. `a,b=(1,2,3)` mismatched count raises ValueError; use `a,*rest`.

questions.answer: Tuple immutability is on references: inner list append mutates the list object, tuple still points to same lists — allowed. Rebinding `data[0]=...` changes the reference — forbidden. List (or tuple containing list) as dict key is unhashable — TypeError.
